value: SF Residential Rent Stabilization and Arbitration Ordinance, Administrative Code Chapter 37 (enacted June 13, 1979)
detail: Administered by the Residential Rent Stabilization and Arbitration Board (Rent Board). The Rent Board notes its online version of the Ordinance is 'not the official record of the laws or regulations of the City and County of San Francisco' - flagged for review.

value: Units built on or before June 13, 1979, not used as a single-family dwelling: 'may have both' rent control and eviction protection
detail: Also subject to exclusions: condos/separately alienable parcels under Costa-Hawkins, post-1979 construction, substantial rehabilitation, and units regulated by another government agency. Verify with the Property Information Map and a Rent Board counselor.

value: 1.6% of base rent, effective March 1, 2026 - February 28, 2027
detail: 60% of the increase in CPI-U for the Bay Area; statutory ceiling of 7%; one increase per 12 months. Prior: 1.4% (2025-26), 1.7% (2024-25).

value: Sec. 37.15 Rent Increase License required before an annual/banked increase can take effect
detail: Generated by annual Housing Inventory reporting. Suspended during noncompliance. Increase effective while unlicensed is null and void.

value: Skipped allowable increases may be accumulated and added, not compounded; no cap; no expiry during a tenancy
detail: Must be broken out in the notice with the dates on which the banked amount is based. Eligibility window conflicts between Rule 4.12 (12 months) and the current sf.gov page (24 months) - flagged.

value: Only via a Rent Board petition for one of six listed grounds, with supporting documentation
detail: Capital improvement, O&M, comparable rents, Proposition I past rent history, utility passthrough, Rule 1.21. Also bond/utility worksheets must be filed before the notice. No filing charge.

value: No increase solely because an occupant was added; no market reset while an original occupant remains
detail: Sec. 37.3(a)(11)(A), 37.3(d)(2)(B), Rules 6.13/6.14. Directly relevant to Unit 1.

value: Tenant Petition for Unlawful Rent Increase (free, no time limit), Tenant Summary Petition, ALJ hearing, appeal
detail: Rent Board also mediates and investigates wrongful eviction claims. It does NOT handle discrimination or retaliation - those go to the SF Human Rights Commission.

value: $59.00 per dwelling unit (2026-27); 50% recoverable from tenant
detail: Separate from the license; due March 1; late penalties apply.

value: SF Human Rights Commission investigates/mediates housing discrimination complaints; California protected classes are enumerated in Government Code 12955(a)
detail: The HRC department page confirms its Civil Rights Division handles housing discrimination complaints; the Rent Board states it does not adjudicate discrimination or retaliation. Protected classes (race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran/military status, genetic information) are from the official statute.

value: Civil Code 1954.50 et seq. allows an owner to set the initial rent for a new tenancy, with exceptions
detail: 1954.53(a)(1): exception where the previous tenancy was terminated by a 1946.1 notice or a change in terms noticed under 827. SF implements this in Sec. 37.3(d) and Rule 6.14. No market-rate increase while an original occupant remains.

value: 5% + CPI or 10%, whichever is lower; 8.8% in San Francisco for 8/1/2026-7/31/2027 - but NOT applicable to SF rent-controlled units
detail: Civil Code 1947.12(d)(3) exempts units already subject to a local ordinance capping increases below 5% + CPI. SF Rent Board: 'This does NOT apply for units under the rent increase limitations of the San Francisco Rent Ordinance.'

value: Civil Code 827: 30 days for <=10%; 90 days if >10% alone or combined within 12 months; mail service per CCP 1013
detail: Applies to both rent-controlled and non-rent-controlled units. sf.gov adds 5 days when mailed.

value: The AB 1482 single-family/condo exemption is unavailable if the owner is a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member
detail: Civil Code 1947.12(d)(5)(A). This is one of the few places where official law distinguishes corporate from individual ownership. Not relevant to a covered multi-unit SF rent-controlled building.

value: Government Code 12955: unlawful to discriminate/harass in housing because of race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran/military status, or genetic information; retaliation prohibited
detail: 12955(f) prohibits harassment, eviction or other discrimination when the dominant purpose is retaliation for exercising rights under the part.

value: 42 USC 3604(b): unlawful to discriminate in the terms, conditions, or privileges of rental because of race, color, religion, sex, familial status, or national origin; 3604(f)(2) covers disability
detail: HUD confirms housing discrimination is illegal in 'nearly all housing, including private housing' and lists the protected classes. Discrimination complaints can be filed with HUD.

topic: Federal rent-increase cap for private, unsubsidized housing
detail: No official federal source located that imposes a numeric cap on rent increases for private, unsubsidized rental housing. Value intentionally left blank and flagged unverified; no inference is drawn. HUD rent rules located apply only to HUD-subsidized/regulated projects.
No official source located stating that federal law preempts or displaces San Francisco's rent increase limits. Value intentionally left blank and flagged unverified.

value: Federal rent-increase rules exist for HUD-regulated/subsidized projects: 'Owners are allowed to charge only the rents shown on the rent schedule ... most recently ... authorized by HUD'
detail: Included only to show that federal rent rules are program-specific to HUD-insured/subsidized projects (HUD Handbook 4350.1 REV-1, Chapter 7, paragraph 7-21), not a general cap on private unsubsidized housing. Whether these units are federally subsidized is not established by any official source; that fact is left unverified.

topic: Additional SF-local protected classes beyond state law
detail: The City's official Analysis of Impediments lists a section 'Other State/Local Protected Classes', but that section's text could not be retrieved in this verification pass. No specific local class is asserted here. Value intentionally left blank and flagged unverified; consult the SF Human Rights Commission.
